paragraphs.source_en: In the spring of Tenshō 1, a season that would mark a turning point in Tokugawa Ieyasu's destiny, Oda Nobunaga faced one crisis after another.

units.source_en: In the spring of Tenshō 1, a season that would mark a turning point in Tokugawa Ieyasu's destiny, Oda Nobunaga faced one crisis after another.
units.source_zh: 对德川家康的命运具有转折意义的天正元年春，织田信长却危机不断。

paragraphs.source_en: As he fretted over the situation, a scout reported, “Takeda Shingen has halted his march on the capital.”

paragraphs.source_en: Once he had assessed the situation, Nobunaga immediately marched to the capital. The weakest link in the encirclement tightening around Nobunaga was undoubtedly Shogun Ashikaga Yoshiaki, who occupied the capital. That accursed bastard! Yet although Nobunaga cursed him bitterly in his heart, after surrounding Nijō Castle he still sent an envoy to declare that he harbored no disloyal intentions.

paragraphs.source_zh: 作出判断后，信长立刻进京了。在对信长形成的包围中，最弱的一个环节，无疑是占据京城的将军足利义昭。这个可恶的浑蛋！信长心里虽然暗恨不已，但在包围二条城之后，他还是派人前去，表明自己并无二心。

paragraphs.source_en: With Yoshiaki under siege, the two sides entered negotiations. Hoping to hold out until Shingen reached the capital, Yoshiaki feigned reconciliation and exchanged vows with Nobunaga.

paragraphs.source_zh: 在义昭被围的情况下，双方举行了谈判。义昭企图坚持到信玄顺利抵京，他故作和好，和信长签订了誓约。

paragraphs.source_en: By the seventh day of the fourth month, Nobunaga had already left Kyoto. Crushing his enemies one by one with lightning speed was his favored strategy. He sent Sakuma Nobumori and Gamō Ujisato against Sasaki Yoshisuke, who was holding out in Namazue Castle in Ōmi, while he himself went to visit Kinoshita Hideyoshi, guardian of the fort on Mount Toragozen, built to defend against Nobunaga's brother-in-law Azai Nagamasa.

units.source_zh: 他派佐久间信盛和蒲生氏乡去攻打困守近江鲶江城的佐佐木义弼，自己则前去看望守卫虎御前山堡垒的木下秀吉，那虎御前山是为了防备妹婿浅井长政而修筑的。

paragraphs.source_zh: 四月初七，信长早已离开京都。以迅雷不及掩耳之势各个击破，是他擅长的策略。他派佐久间信盛和蒲生氏乡去攻打困守近江鲶江城的佐佐木义弼，自己则前去看望守卫虎御前山堡垒的木下秀吉，那虎御前山是为了防备妹婿浅井长政而修筑的。

paragraphs.source_en: On the evening of the ninth day of the fourth month, “Monkey” Kinoshita Hideyoshi, now lord of Nagahama with an income of fifty thousand koku, had just finished an exercise in attacking Odani Castle with his prized retainers Katō Toranosuke, Katagiri Sukesaku, Fukushima Ichimatsu, and Ishida Sakichi, and was listening to Takenaka Hanbei's critique.

paragraphs.source_en: Nobunaga handed the reins to an attendant and gazed at the stout fort built directly opposite Odani Castle, unable to keep from frowning. He was not dissatisfied with Hideyoshi's design. A loud shout from here could be heard distinctly by those inside Odani Castle. Remembering that his sister and three beloved nieces still lived there, Nobunaga ground his teeth in hatred of the foolish Nagamasa and his father.
